# Block 2: Inline completions {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| include: false
source("R/booktem_setup.R")
source("R/my_setup.R")
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(webexercises)
```


Inline completion is the simplest kind of `r glossary("assistant")`: grey
"ghost text" appears as you type, and you accept it with Tab, reject it with
Esc, or carry on typing. By the end of this block you will know how to get
useful suggestions every time: write a specific comment just before the cursor.

Claude Code has no inline completion, so this is the one block where GitHub
Copilot is the main tool.

*⏱ ~25 minutes*


## Setup

You signed in to GitHub Copilot in the pre-work
([Setting up Claude Code](11a-setup-claude-code.qmd), Step 7). Check it still
works: in a blank R script, type `# Calculate the mean of 1 to 100`. Within a
few seconds you should see ghost text such as `mean(1:100)`; if not, press
Enter and wait.

**If no ghost text appears,** follow the instructor's screen for this block and
fix the set-up at the break.

:::{.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Set-up routes, plans and data

- **RStudio:** enable GitHub Copilot in RStudio's options and sign in to
  GitHub.
- **Positron:** choose GitHub Copilot as the completions provider (see
  Positron's completions documentation).
- **VS Code:** select **Use AI Features** from the Copilot icon in the Status
  Bar and sign in with GitHub.

Copilot Free allows a limited number of completions per month (2,000 at the
time of writing); paid plans do not meter them. Completions send the code
around your cursor to the provider, so the disclosure points in
[Block 4](11d-context-disclosure-autonomy.qmd) apply here too. Use one
completion provider at a time, so you know which tool made each suggestion.
:::

:::{.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Using Posit Assistant

In RStudio and Positron you can use Posit AI Next Edit Suggestions instead:
in RStudio, turn it on from the Posit Assistant toolbar button (it needs a
Posit AI account); in Positron, choose it as the completions provider. Posit AI
does not meter completions.
:::


## The context principle

A suggestion can only use what is in the model's
`r glossary("context window")` when it is made. Copilot fills that window mainly
from the current file, and above all from the comment just before the cursor.
In Positron and VS Code it may also use other open tabs. It does not see your R
session.

:::{.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Using Posit Assistant

Posit AI Next Edit Suggestions also sees your live R session: the columns of
loaded data frames, the functions you have defined and the packages you have
loaded. What you have loaded becomes one more lever.
:::


## Activity: The context demonstration

:::{.task}
::::{.task-header}
The context demonstration (10 minutes)
::::
::::{.task-container}

**Start state:** your workshop repository is open, and the set-up check produced
ghost text.

The data are `voles_metabolism.csv`: a synthetic trial in 72 voles, with
columns `subject_id`, `sex`, `treatment_arm`, `mass_pre_g`, `mass_post_g` and
`metabolic_rate_post`. The names were chosen so that no model has seen them
before.

**1. No context.** Restart R, so you are in a
`r glossary("fresh R session")`, and open a blank R script. Type only this
comment, and wait.

**In the R script:**

```{r}
#| eval: false
# calculate the mean change in mass by treatment
```

Note the suggestion. With no data and no column names in view, the model has
to guess.

**2. Context in the file.** In a new blank script, type the lines below
down to `glimpse(voles)`, and run them, so that `voles` is loaded. Then type
the same comment on a new line, and wait.

**In the R script:**

```{r}
#| eval: false
# Voles metabolism trial: effect of treatment on body mass
# 72 voles, three treatment arms (Control, Low_dose, High_dose), two sexes
# Native pipe |>, tidyverse

library(tidyverse)

voles <- read_csv(here::here("data", "raw", "voles_metabolism.csv"))
glimpse(voles)

# calculate the mean change in mass by treatment
```

`r hide("A typical good result")`

```{r, eval = FALSE}
voles |>
  mutate(mass_change_g = mass_post_g - mass_pre_g) |>
  summarise(
    mean_change = mean(mass_change_g, na.rm = TRUE),
    .by = treatment_arm
  )
```

The exact form varies between people and sessions.

`r unhide()`

Compare the two suggestions. Did the second use real column names? Did it
compute post minus pre?

**You are done when** you can say what the second suggestion had that the
first did not.

**If it goes wrong:** if no suggestion appears, type the comment again on a new
line; if the script stops running, *Session → Restart R* and run it from the
top.

::::
:::

:::{.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Using Posit Assistant: context in the session

With Posit AI Next Edit Suggestions, keep `voles` loaded from step 2, then type
only the comment from step 1 in a new blank script. If the suggestion now uses the real column names, it
came from your session, not from the file.
:::


## Activity: Build a small analysis

:::{.task}
::::{.task-header}
Build a small analysis (10 minutes)
::::
::::{.task-container}

**Start state:** the script from step 2, with `voles` loaded.

For each step, write the comment first, then accept, modify or reject the
suggestion, and note which you did. The note is what makes you notice an
unchecked acceptance.

**1. Summary table.** The mean and standard deviation of `mass_change_g` by
`treatment_arm` and `sex`, with the number of observations per cell. (Create
`mass_change_g` first if your script does not have it.)

**2. Plot.** `mass_change_g` against `metabolic_rate_post`, coloured by
`treatment_arm`.

**You are done when** a fresh R session (*Session → Restart R*, then run the
script from the top) produces the table and the plot without error.

**If it goes wrong:** delete the last suggestion you accepted, and write a more
specific comment naming the data frame and its columns.

`r hide("An example")`

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# Voles metabolism trial: effect of treatment on body mass
library(tidyverse)
library(here)

voles <- read_csv(
  here("data", "raw", "voles_metabolism.csv"),
  col_types = cols(
    subject_id = col_character(),
    sex = col_character(),
    treatment_arm = col_character(),
    mass_pre_g = col_double(),
    mass_post_g = col_double(),
    metabolic_rate_post = col_double()
  )
) |>
  mutate(mass_change_g = mass_post_g - mass_pre_g)

# mean and SD of mass_change_g by treatment_arm and sex, with n per cell
voles |>
  summarise(
    mean_change_g = mean(mass_change_g),
    sd_change_g = sd(mass_change_g),
    n = n(),
    .by = c(treatment_arm, sex)
  ) |>
  arrange(treatment_arm, sex)

# mass_change_g against metabolic_rate_post, coloured by treatment_arm
ggplot(voles, aes(metabolic_rate_post, mass_change_g, colour = treatment_arm)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(x = "Metabolic rate (post-treatment)", y = "Change in mass (g)")
```

The plot drops the one animal with no metabolic rate and says so in a warning:
read it rather than ignore it.

`r unhide()`

::::
:::


:::{.callout-note}
## Check · Reproduce · Record

- **You can now:** steer inline completion with a specific comment and the
  right code above the cursor, **trusted because** you decided on every
  suggestion and the script runs from a fresh R session.
- **Check:** accept, modify or reject every suggestion deliberately.
- **Reproduce:** good suggestions come from context in the file or session, so
  keep that context in the script, where it reruns.
- **Record:** nothing to log yet; your `r glossary("AI-use log")` starts in
  [Block 4](11d-context-disclosure-autonomy.qmd), once an
  `r glossary("agent")` starts doing work.
:::


## Check your understanding

**The single most reliable way to improve inline suggestions in a new script
is to:**

`r longmcq(c(
  "Switch to a different underlying model",
  "Open more files in the editor as additional context",
  answer = "Write a specific comment immediately before the code you want, naming the data frame and its columns",
  "Restart the IDE so the assistant has a fresh context"
))`

**You get correct column names in a blank script using Posit AI Next Edit
Suggestions, but not with Copilot. The most likely reason is:**

`r longmcq(c(
  "Posit AI uses a larger model",
  answer = "Next Edit Suggestions can see the data frame loaded in your R session; Copilot sees only the files",
  "Copilot cannot read R code",
  "The column names were in Posit AI's training data"
))`


## Going further (not covered live)

This material is not covered in the live session. Work through it afterwards if
it is useful to you.

:::{.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## The full four-step analysis

The live activity uses two of four steps. The full sequence, again writing the
comment for each step before accepting, rejecting or modifying the suggestion:

1. Filter to subjects with non-missing `metabolic_rate_post` and create a
   derived variable `mass_change_g`.
2. Produce a summary table of the mean and standard deviation of
   `mass_change_g` by `treatment_arm` and `sex`, with the number of
   observations per cell.
3. Fit a linear model of `metabolic_rate_post` on `treatment_arm` and `sex`.
   Inspect the coefficients.
4. Produce one plot relating `mass_change_g` to `metabolic_rate_post`,
   coloured by `treatment_arm`.

When you have finished steps 2 and 4, post the code Copilot suggested for
step 4 in the Zoom chat, with a note on whether you accepted, changed or
rejected it. Then compare with what others posted: the comparison usually shows
different suggestions, different acceptance decisions and, often, different bugs.
:::
